fixture_name: NE Edmonton Ring Road planning-stage RSA — Canada TAC planning (real sample, Alberta Transportation 2009)
subject: judge-baseline

justifications.substance: Sub-preferred systems-service spacing (1970 m/1670 m vs 3000 m) placing service interchanges inside the system interchange's functional area, with listed weaving pairs, is a core planning-stage geometric/functional safety concern with a credible rear-end/sideswipe mechanism.
justifications.evidence_grounding: EV-CA-039 provides a verbatim quote directly supporting the pivotal spacing/functional-area claim, EV-CA-003 grounds the network-wide consequence propagation, assumptions cite recorded input categories, and inference over staging data is explicitly labelled in confidence.
justifications.jurisdiction_correctness: Framed purely as a safety_concern treating 'preferred' spacing deviation as a risk driver rather than a mandatory-standard breach, keeping the safety question categorically distinct from any compliance assertion, consistent with CRSAG planning-stage semantics.
justifications.recommendation_quality: Dual-path recommendation (re-space to 3000 m in next functional-plan iteration OR insert collector-distributor roadways) is specific, stage-appropriate, and viable, with a concrete verification step against 2041 staging-year weave volumes.
justifications.vru_coverage: VRUs are genuinely not applicable on the fully access-controlled mainline, and the finding explicitly acknowledges this and scopes road users to vehicle occupants, satisfying the acknowledge-non-applicability criterion.
